def-td-macro-versus-micro-entropy-claim.physical_scope: Definitions of the adopted macroscopic equilibrium entropy and selected finite-model microscopic entropy quantities; no identity between these quantities is asserted without a separately specified equilibrium bridge.

def-td-macro-versus-micro-entropy-claim:
## Definition

Fix a material constitution $c$ and its equilibrium state domain $D_c$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. The adopted macroscopic entropy is the finite state function $S_c:D_c\to\mathbb R$ of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], with values in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ under [[def-td-si-quantities]]. Its argument is an equilibrium macrostate. The definition does not assign $S_c$ to an arbitrary nonequilibrium configuration or to a microscopic trajectory.

For a finite microstate model, use a nonempty labelled set $\Omega_N=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N\}$, $N\ge1$, and an assigned energy map $E:\Omega_N\to\mathbb R$ with values in joules, as in the planned TD8 interface of page `td-finite-statistical-bridge`. A chosen coarse-graining is a finite label set $\mathcal M$ and a map $\pi:\Omega_N\to\mathcal M$. For $m\in\mathcal M$, let $M_m=\{\omega_i:\pi(\omega_i)=m\}$ and let $N_m$ be the number of indices in this set. Only labels with $N_m\ge1$ are admitted here. The Boltzmann macrocell entropy of this specified coarse-graining is

$$S_{\mathrm B}(m):=k_{\mathrm B}\log N_m.$$

For a specified probability vector $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_N)$, where $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^N p_i=1$, define its Gibbs–Shannon entropy by

$$S_{\mathrm G}(p):=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_{i=1}^N p_i\log p_i,$$

with the summand $p_i\log p_i$ defined to be $0$ when $p_i=0$. Both expressions have units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, because their logarithms are dimensionless and $k_{\mathrm B}$ has those units. The finite sum and logarithm have the meanings of [[def-finite-sum]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]].

For a density operator $\rho$ in the declared finite-dimensional sector class of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], its von Neumann physical entropy is $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho)=k_{\mathrm B}s(\rho)$, with $s(\rho)$ the dimensionless entropy defined there. That supplier defines no such quantity for its infinite-dimensional spatial sectors.

These are distinct definitions on different domains: $S_c$ acts on an equilibrium macrostate, $S_{\mathrm B}$ on a chosen macrocell, $S_{\mathrm G}$ on a specified probability vector, and $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ on a finite-sector density operator. A numerical equality among them requires an additional, explicit identification of model, coarse-graining, preparation and applicable limit. This item supplies no such identification and adopts no canonical or microcanonical sampling rule.

pthm-td-unitary-entropy-invariance.physical_scope: The exact closed, finite-dimensional sector model and unitary dynamics of the named NRQM supplier, including its adopted canonical preparation and stated choice assumptions; the result identifies no macroscopic entropy, open-system relaxation, or laboratory behaviour.

pthm-td-unitary-entropy-invariance:
## Statement

Adopt exactly the state, observable, autonomous-dynamics and canonical-ensemble assumptions, readings, finite-dimensional sector class, and normalized canonical preparation of [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]]. The sector $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its self-adjoint energy operator $H_N^\sigma$ are those of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. Model time $t$ is in seconds, $H_N^\sigma$ is in joules, and $\hbar=h/(2\pi)$ is the reduced Planck constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The evolution definition [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] gives $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^*$. Both the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Define $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho)=k_{\mathrm B}s(\rho)$ as in [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Then, for every declared sector preparation $\rho(0)$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$:

1. $S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(t))=S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho(0))$;
2. the adopted canonical preparation is stationary; and
3. a preparation different from the canonical one is never mapped to it by this unitary flow.

These are statements about the exact closed finite-sector model. They do not identify $S_{\mathrm{vN}}$ with the macroscopic equilibrium entropy $S_c$ of [[def-td-macro-versus-micro-entropy-claim]], derive the canonical preparation, or establish bath relaxation or thermalization.
